---
title: Typed negative claims
description: Deliver library-written statements for none, not-found and complete claims, with the search scope and gaps preserved.
---

`.negativeClaims()` makes the library write a typed negative statement from the
searches the answer cites. The model chooses `kind`, `about` and `restsOn`; it does
not write the scope, gaps or delivered statement.

`NegativeClaimsOptions` configures the field, eligible tools and failure behavior.
`NegativeClaimCitation` is the model-input shape; `DeliveredNegative` adds the
library's statement and version. `agent.answerNegatives()` returns the
`AnswerNegatives` metadata with per-source checked counts, diagnostics and
dispatched action outcomes; an action outcome does not prove an external effect.

The structured path is **unmeasured**. Typed enforcement is **available, not
recommended** until its benchmark gates pass. Other fields remain unchecked model
text. A bounded English grammar observes the model's original strings and files
findings; it never blocks delivery or verifies prose. `prose`, `strictProse` and
`enforceProse` options are refused: observation is automatic, enforcement unavailable.

## Declare the search and bind the caller

Use a local tool with a [search declaration](/docs/build/tools#coverage-composed-from-the-call--search).
The declaration must describe the query the tool actually runs. Fill caller scope
through `hostFilled` from the host's authenticated identity, rather than asking the
model to supply it. A local `absent({ among })` result can also support a named miss.
MCP and ToolProvider declarations cannot establish a typed negative.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="search"
  title="A caller-scoped search with an explicit source gap"
/>

An empty result is different from an unread search: a completed search can find
zero rows. Missing observations, skipped checks and missing caller scope remain
unverified. A declaration that misdescribes the backend is outside this check's
guarantee; declarations and the host's identity are the trusted inputs.

## Give the model a citation field

The field must be a required top-level array. Each entry requires `kind`, `about`
and `restsOn`. Supply `jsonSchema` explicitly or use a parser that provides
`toJsonSchema()`; the library does not infer a shape by executing a parser.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="schema"
  title="The model supplies citations, without statement text"
/>

The library serves the short-handle pattern `^r[1-9][0-9]{0,3}$`, limits the field
to 32 claims and each citation to 16 reads, and closes each entry to extra fields.
The model receives handles such as `r1` beside admitted results. Provider call IDs
never select evidence. `about` must match every cited population and each read must
be within the admitted caller scope.

| Kind        | What the cited reads must establish                                                                                                       |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `none`      | A declared absence within the composed search scope.                                                                                      |
| `not-found` | A named miss from `absent({ among })`, with the inventory's limits.                                                                       |
| `complete`  | Completeness for the executed arguments, without an open page, reached cap or partial result. The statement describes rows actually read. |

## Deliver the statement and its marker together

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts"
  region="configure"
  title="Deliver the library statement"
/>

An established entry gains `statement`, `delivery: 'record-composed'` and `version`.
Display that marker beside the sentence. The delivered `about` keeps the original
model string or number, so app comparisons still work. Only the library sentence
quotes and sanitizes values; `about` is not an evidence identity. The answer-level delivery is
`as-checked` only when its sole field consists of established library statements;
any other field makes it `recorded`. That marker never verifies surrounding model
text. The model-input parser describes only
citations; `runTyped()` returns the enriched delivered object without running that
parser over it again.

Every execution mode delivers the library statement, including when an app's
`.answerValidation()` uses observe mode. The final answer is buffered so a draft
cannot escape through streaming. The person, `turn_end.answerNegatives`, conversation
history and memory receive the same statements and gaps.

`unestablished` chooses the failure behavior:

| Setting              | Delivery                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `withhold` (default) | Withhold the whole answer; the caller receives `AnswerValidationError`, HTTP hosts return 422 and AG-UI reports `RUN_ERROR`.     |
| `state-searched`     | Replace the entry with what the admitted record says was searched and any admitted contrary result. The failed or unverified standing stays failed or unverified. |

A contrary read is named by its result handle and shows bounded, quoted native
row values when they survived middleware, placement and truncation unchanged.
Otherwise its count is reported without re-exposing hidden values. A positive
result without a coverage declaration is explicitly labelled that way.

A bad citation gets one correction request naming valid handles, with no tools
available. If `.outputSchema()` enables retries, schema correction shares that
same one-request budget with citation and evidence correction, even when `retries`
is greater than one. Rejected drafts and correction instructions stay out of
conversation history and memory. A correction cannot repeat a write to satisfy
the checker. A later dispatched
call that may write invalidates an earlier read even if the call fails; a local
`effects: 'read'` declaration can identify a read-only tool. Remote read-only hints
cannot. Reads retained through a pause remain eligible within the same turn;
earlier-turn reads are stale and their refusal identifies the earlier turn and recorded date.

This does not verify the rest of an answer. An empty citation array makes no typed
claim. Every original free-form model string, including nested fields and `about`, is observed
before the library writes its statements. Detected negatives file `negative-claim`
findings; unread units file `negative-claim-note` findings. Both make the answer
fold not-sure, without changing delivery. The grammar has known false positives and
misses; prose remains unchecked even when it produces no finding.

The whole answer is limited to 65,536 UTF-16 code units and 256 string values for
observation, and 32 detected claims or unjudged units for observation. Exceeding a budget produces one
whole-answer `input-limit` or `too-many-claims` note without checking evidence.
The model is instructed to state negatives only through cited searches. These
instructions do not guarantee compliance.

The global answer-account `templateVersion` changes from 11 to 12, including for
agents without `.negativeClaims()`. Consumers must tolerate the new version and
`negative-prose-unverified` assessment reason.

 The checker
compares other observations only within its declared subject and scope rules.
Independent host-authored answer checks continue to apply, and a library statement
never turns an unverified answer into a verified one.

The mock example runs without credentials or network access:

```sh
npm run example -- examples/features/110-negative-claims.ts
```
